title: The scorecard's idle hours card says owner work for a mission with no backlog, and flags only backlog missions idle
prompt:
Read crates/spawn-postgres/src/experience.rs (the `missions` rows behind `/api/scorecard/fleet`), crates/spawn-cli/src/scorecard/fleet.rs (`idle`: the idle flag of a mission's row), web/src/fleetDecisions.ts (`decisionsFromApi`, `idleHoursByMission`) and web/src/components/scorecard/FleetDecisions.tsx (the "Idle hours by mission" card), and what makes a mission take its work from a backlog (`objectives` on its `mission.configured` record).

The problem, as the owner reads the Scorecard after 73e3596d (lead-mac, sync/queue.md 23:45; sync/page-scorecard-2026-11-11-2336.png). The card's only two badges flag the two owner-work missions idle: #7 at 107 / 144 h (75%) and #8 at 106 / 140 h (76%). Their work comes from the owner when there is some, so an hour with no task there is no fault. The live `/api/scorecard/fleet?window=7d` says `"idle": true` for 7 and 8 and false for 4 (63 / 168 h) and 6 (61 / 151 h). Those are the backlog missions whose idle hours are the fleet's real loss (objective 058). The card points the owner at the wrong missions.

Required behaviour.
(a) Every `missions` row of `/api/scorecard/fleet` carries `owner_work`: true for a mission with no objective backlog, false for one that has one.
(b) An owner-work row is never `idle`. A backlog mission's `idle` is as today.
(c) web/src/fleetDecisions.ts: `decisionsFromApi(answer).idleHoursByMission` rows carry `ownerWork` beside `idle`. The card says "owner work" for such a row, where it would have flagged it idle, and keeps its idle hours.
(d) fleetDecisions.ts keeps loading with node alone.

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/062.sh. Records are written through `spawn_control_record`, and `spawn serve` answers. Missions 1 and 3 take their work from a backlog; mission 2 is owner work (accept review, no backlog). Mission 3 has a task in work all along; 1 and 2 have none. Read through `GET /api/scorecard/fleet?window=24h`:
- (1) Mission 2's row is {idle false, owner_work true}, mission 1's is {idle true, owner_work false}, and mission 3's is {idle false, owner_work false}.
- (2) Under node, decisionsFromApi over the answer gives rows whose [idle, ownerWork] are [true, false] for 1, [false, true] for 2 and [false, false] for 3.
It fails with 1 on 73e3596d: the rows have no `owner_work`, mission 2 is flagged idle, and the card's rows have no `ownerWork`.

The product reason. Idle hours are only a loss where work was waiting to be done. Flagging the owner's own missions idle trains the owner to ignore the badge, and the badge is exactly what should pull the eye to a backlog mission without work. Saying "owner work" keeps the badge a signal.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/, web/test/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base, any lint relaxation and any build-time code. The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host. Keep every existing check green and add tests of your own for the new behaviour: a fleet.rs unit test that an owner-work row is never idle and a backlog row is as before, a spawn-postgres test of `owner_work` through the real store, and web/test tests for (c).
